blocks.text: The hall of the Gibichungs on the Rhine. This is quite open at the back. An open shore stretching to the river occupies the background. Rocky heights enclose the shore. Gunther and Gutrune on a throne at one side, before which stands a table with drinking-vessels on it. In front of this Hagen is seated.

lines: Is my fame on the Rhine
To me by Grimhild’ our mother.
That the Gibichung has not yet won.
Whom wouldst thou have me woo,
Her chamber is circled by fire;
And he who would Brünnhild’ woo
Must break through the daunting flame.
Suffices my strength for the task?
For one stronger still it is decreed.
Had as their offspring this child.
In the woods he grew and waxed strong.
Tell me what deed of high valour
Made this hero the first in renown.
The fame of the hero dawned.
They say that a priceless treasure
The Niblungs had in their hoard.
The man who could use its spell
Were lord of the world evermore.
And Siegfried won it in fight?
He has the Niblungs in thrall.
And Brünnhild’ no other can win?
To no other will the flames yield.

blocks.text: He walks to and fro much agitated.
Without leaving his seat causes Gunther to pull up as he approaches him, by a gesture of mysterious import.

lines: Were she by Siegfried brought home?
But how could I force this man
To woo the bride for me?
Thy simple prayer would force him,
What arts have I to bind him?
Has long ere this by the fairest
What of the drink in the chest?
In me who won it have more faith.
To thee in love it will bind
Him whom thy heart most desires.

blocks.text: Gunther has come to the table again, and, leaning against it, pays close attention.

lines: And taste of this potion of herbs,
He would straight forget he had looked
Who for brother gave us thee.
But how can he be found?

blocks.text: A horn on the stage, from the background on the left, very loud but distant.

lines: Belike in his chase he will come
To the Gibich’s realm on the Rhine.

blocks.text: A horn on the stage, nearer, but still distant. Both listen.

lines: A horn from the Rhine I hear.

blocks.text: Looks down the river and calls towards the back.

lines: A man and horse on board a boat!
His horn how gaily he winds!

blocks.text: A horn on the stage sounds nearer. Gunther stops half-way listening.
Making a trumpet of his hands, calls towards the river.

lines: I seek the son of Gibich.
I bid thee welcome to Gunther’s hall.

blocks.text: Siegfried in a boat appears at the shore.

lines: This way! Stop here and land!

blocks.text: Siegfried brings his boat to the shore. Hagen makes it fast with the chain. Siegfried springs ashore with his horse. Gunther has come down and joined Hagen.
Gutrune gazes at Siegfried from the throne in astonishment. Gunther prepares to offer him friendly greetings. All stand fixed in silent mutual contemplation.
Leaning on his horse, remains quietly standing by the boat.

lines: I am he thou dost seek.

blocks.text: As he hands over the horse to Hagen.

Hagen leads the horse away. While Siegfried looks thoughtfully after him, Gutrune, obeying a sign of Hagen’s which Siegfried does not notice, goes to her room through a door on the left. Gunther comes into the hall with Siegfried, whom he has invited to accompany him.

lines: By my body I swear it!
Nor land nor folk have I to give,
As I live it grows less.
Let my sword be my witness!—

blocks.text: Who has come back and now stands behind Siegfried.

lines: So lightly I prize its worth.
I left it lying in a cavern,
Where a dragon once held watch.
Only this, not knowing its use.
The gem of the Nibelung’s art;
Its use, when worn on thy head,
Is to change thy shape as thou wilt;
If fain to be borne afar,
In a flash lo! thou art there!
Nay, Siegfried, let us not barter;
All I have a bauble poor,
Matched with thy treasure, would be.
I will serve thee without reward.

blocks.text: Hagen has gone to Gutrune’s door, and now opens it.
Enters carrying a full drinking-horn, with which she approaches Siegfried.

lines: ’Tis his daughter gives thee to drink.

blocks.text: Bows in a friendly manner and takes the horn, which he holds thoughtfully before him.
He puts the drinking-horn to his lips and takes a long draught; then he hands it back to Gutrune, who, ashamed and confused, casts down her eyes. Siegfried gazes at her with sudden passion.

lines: Why sink them abashed by my gaze?

blocks.text: Gutrune, blushing, looks up at him.

lines: They kindle my blood; it flows
Gunther, what name is thy sister’s?
That in her eyes I am reading?
With thy brother I was fain to serve;
Were I to pray the same of thee,
Wouldst thou like him be proud?

blocks.text: Gutrune involuntarily meets Hagen’s eye. She bows her head humbly, and, expressing her feeling of unworthiness with a gesture, leaves the hall with faltering steps.
Attentively watched by Hagen and Gunther, gazes after Gutrune as if entranced.

lines: My heart on one I have set
Whom there is no way to win.
He only who braves the fire...

blocks.text: As if making an intense effort to remember something.
Siegfried shows by a gesture that at the mention of Brünnhilde’s name all remembrance of her has faded.

lines: I dare not essay the dread mountain;
The flames would not fall for me.

blocks.text: Awakes from his dreamy state, and turns to Gunther high-spirited and gay.

lines: For thee I will win her,
Of fire I have no fear;
If Gutrun’ I win as my wife.
Then let the oath now be sworn!

blocks.text: Hagen fills a drinking-horn with fresh wine; he holds it out to Siegfried and Gunther, who cut their arms with their swords and hold them for a short pace over the horn; then they each lay two fingers on the horn, which Hagen continues to hold between them.

lines: Lo! I drop in the horn!
Bloom our blood in the draught!
Troth I drink to the friend

blocks.text: Gunther drinks and hands the horn to Siegfried, who finishes the draught, and holds out the empty horn to Hagen. Hagen breaks the horn in two with his sword. Gunther and Siegfried join hands.
Observes Hagen, who, while the oath was being sworn, has stood behind him.

lines: Why hast not thou plighted thy troth?
My blood had soured the good draught.
Heed not him and his spleen.

blocks.text: He steps nearer to Gunther and points at him.

lines: And then bring home the bride.

blocks.text: He turns to go, and beckons Gunther to follow him.

lines: I am eager to be back.

blocks.text: He goes to the shore to unmoor the boat.

lines: Thou, Hagen, keep guard o’er the homestead.

blocks.text: He follows Siegfried to the shore. Whilst Siegfried and Gunther, after laying their arms in the boat, are hoisting the sail and making ready for departure, Hagen takes up his spear and shield. Gutrune appears at the door of her chamber just as Siegfried is pushing off the boat, which immediately glides into the middle of the stream.
While he seats himself comfortably with shield and spear in front of the hall.

lines: For wife seeking to win thee!

blocks.text: She returns to her room greatly excited. Siegfried has seized an oar and rows the boat down-stream, so that it is soon lost to view.
Sits motionless, his back against the door-post of the hall.

lines: Warding the hall from the foe;
And sails away for a wife;
And danger braves for his sake;
With her he brings me—the ring.
Gaily speed on in your pride!

blocks.text: A curtain which frames the front of the hall is drawn, and cuts the stage off from the audience.

The curtain is raised again. The rocky height as in the Prelude. Brünnhilde sits at the entrance to the cave in silent contemplation of Siegfried’s ring. Moved by blissful memories, she covers the ring with kisses. Distant thunder is heard; she looks up and listens. She turns to the ring again. A flash of lightning. Again she listens, and looks into the distance, whence a dark thunder-cloud is approaching the rock.

lines: Who seeks the lonely one here?

blocks.text: Calling to the wing, and then hastening to the edge of the rock.

lines: And leave thy courser to rest.

blocks.text: She runs into the wood, from which a loud sound like a thunder-clap is heard. She returns in great agitation with Waltraute, and remains joyfully excited without noticing the latter’s anxious fear.

lines: And I know that his anger
Here to the rock I was bound,
Doomed to be thrall to the man
Who should wake the maid as he passed,
To bar to all cowards the road.
In light and laughter I live.

blocks.text: She embraces Waltraute with wild manifestations of joy, which the latter tries with anxious impatience to repress.

lines: Hast thou been lured by my lot,
Far other the cause why I come,

blocks.text: Here, for the first time, notices with surprise Waltraute’s wildly excited state.

lines: So the stern one does not forgive?
At an end were my distress.
Mark with care what I say!
Drives me back to Walhall again.
What ails, then, the Gods everlasting?
Give earnest heed to what I tell thee!
He wandered and roamed through the world.
A hero had cleft it asunder.
The logs as they hewed them,
High round the hall of the blest.
Who gathered in fear sit beside him.
The hall, ranged round in their order.
She would restore the ring that was theirs.
Both God and world were freed!”
And stormed in tumult to thee.
End thou the grief of the Gods!

blocks.text: She has thrown herself down before Brünnhilde.

lines: Sad one, are those thou dost tell?
I grasp not what thou art saying;
What wouldst thou, wild one, of me?
To the Rhine-daughters give it again.
The accurst thing cast in the waves!
Ha! dost thou know what ’twould mean?
Much is the fame of the Gods;
One glance at its shining gold,
One flash of its sacred fire
Than bliss of all the Gods
Shines from it bright and blessèd.
Ah, could I but utter the rapture
Repeat what I have told thee
That love I will not forswear,
Of love they never shall rob me;
Thus coldly thou leavest thy sister?
I will not part with the ring.

blocks.text: She rushes away. A storm-cloud immediately rises from the wood, accompanied by thunder.
As she looks after the brightly lit, retreating thunder-cloud, which soon vanishes in the distance.

lines: And may I see thee no more!

blocks.text: Twilight has fallen. The light of the fire gradually shines more brightly from below. She gazes quietly out on the landscape.

lines: The flames that encircle me glow.

blocks.text: The firelight approaches from below. Ever-brightening tongues of flame shoot up over the edge of the rock.

lines: The billows that blaze round the rock?

blocks.text: Siegfried’s horn is heard from the valley. Brünnhilde starts up in delight.

lines: With his horn greeting he sends!

blocks.text: She hastens joyfully to the edge of the crag. Flames leap up, out of which Siegfried springs forward on to a high rock, whereupon the flames immediately withdraw and again only shine up from below. Brünnhilde recoils in terror, flies to the foreground, and from there, in speechless astonishment, stares at Siegfried, who, wearing the Tarnhelm, which covers the upper half of his face, leaving only his eyes free, appears in Gunther’s form.
Remaining on the rock at the back, motionless and leaning on his shield, regards Brünnhilde. In a feigned (harsher) voice.

lines: Whom thy fire did not dismay.
I want thee for my wife;
Thy pride by force at need.

blocks.text: As before, beginning with a slightly tremulous voice, but continuing with more confidence.
Springs down from the stone and approaches.
Stretching out with a threatening gesture the finger on which she wears Siegfried’s ring.

lines: Stand back! Fear thou this token!
While I am shielded by this,
Thou canst not force me to shame.
Wife it shall make thee to Gunther;
With this ring thou shalt be wed.
Nor dare, overbold, to draw near!

blocks.text: He presses towards her. There is a struggle. Brünnhilde wrenches herself free, flies and turns round as if to defend herself. Siegfried seizes her again. She flies; he reaches her. They wrestle violently together. Siegfried catches her hand and draws the ring from her finger. She gives a loud scream. As she sinks helpless into his arms her unconscious look meets Siegfried’s eyes. Siegfried lays her fainting on the stone bench at the entrance to the cave.

lines: Lead me the way to thy cave!

blocks.text: Stares, as if fainting, before her; exhausted.
Drives her on with a gesture of command. Trembling and with tottering steps she goes into the cave. In his natural voice.

lines: And loyal been to my brother;
Lie betwixt me and his bride!

blocks.text: He follows Brünnhilde. The curtain falls.
